content: The Pacific Physical Activity and Sedentary Behaviour Guidelines emphasize the critical role of physical activity in maintaining and improving health across all age groups. Regular physical activity is essential for preventing and managing various health conditions, enhancing mood and sleep, increasing energy levels, and supporting healthy aging. Globally, a significant portion of the population does not meet the recommended levels of physical activity, contributing to the rising burden of obesity and non-communicable diseases (NCDs). Physical inactivity is one of the leading risk factors for NCDs, alongside unhealthy diets, tobacco use, and harmful alcohol consumption. Meeting global physical activity recommendations could prevent 4 to 5 million deaths annually. Modernization and mechanization have made daily life more convenient but have also reduced opportunities for physical activity, promoting sedentary behaviors such as prolonged sitting and screen time. These behaviors are associated with poor health outcomes. The guidelines provide evidence-based recommendations to help individuals incorporate sufficient physical activity into their lives and reduce sedentary behavior to improve overall health. For adults, engaging in at least 150–300 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic physical activity per week is recommended, with additional health benefits gained from higher levels of activity. Activities should include muscle-strengthening exercises involving major muscle groups at least twice a week. Older adults are encouraged to include balance and coordination exercises to prevent falls and maintain functional abilities. For children and adolescents, at least 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity daily is advised, with a focus on aerobic activities and activities that strengthen muscles and bones. The guidelines also address specific populations, including pregnant and postpartum women, individuals with disabilities, and those with chronic diseases. Pregnant women are encouraged to engage in at least 30 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity on most days of the week, which can reduce the risk of complications such as gestational diabetes and postpartum depression. Children under five years old should engage in active play throughout the day, with screen time limited to less than one hour for those aged 1–4 years and none for infants under one year. The guidelines highlight the importance of starting small for those who are not currently active and gradually increasing activity levels. Any amount of physical activity is better than none, and even low-intensity activities can provide health benefits. The recommendations are adaptable to individual needs and circumstances, ensuring inclusivity for people of all abilities and health conditions. In summary, the Pacific Physical Activity and Sedentary Behaviour Guidelines provide practical, evidence-based strategies to promote physical activity and reduce sedentary behavior, ultimately improving health outcomes and preventing NCDs. These guidelines serve as a foundation for health education, policy development, and environmental changes to support active lifestyles.
